findings.5_assertion_quality: The rows are capable of failing for the reason they state, where they carry the card. R-A reddened 10 ids and R-B reddened 8, reproducing the executor's M2 and M6 row counts (15/14 and 17/16) exactly, which is strong evidence their matrix is a measurement rather than a narrative. Parts their matrix did not cover, measured here: (i) the grant checks on the other five entry points - they WORK (403 FORBIDDEN each) but neutralising all five leaves 24/24 green, so they are entirely unasserted; (ii) the limit-above-200 refusals on both read paths - they WORK (400) and raising the threshold reddens nothing; (iii) the cross-project branch - it is not NOT_FOUND at all: under this card's single-project grant model the grant check fires first and answers 403, so the disclosure names a shadowed branch while the reachable, unasserted ones are unknown-session 404 (correct on all four paths) and the runState 404 for a session pointing at a vanished run row (reachable and correct, because OpenClientSession accepts a dangling run_id - the index only requires a Project row); (iv) the sealed-session gate on the WRITE path - it WORKS (409) and is unasserted, only the takeover copy is covered. Three rows are weaker than they look: INDEX-SUBSTRATE-GAP-MEASURED compares fixtureProjectRows with itself, so the Project-row half can never fail; RACE-LOSER-CANNOT-WRITE hard-codes STALE_WRITER_EPOCH at epoch 2, which only holds when both claims land (measured landed=2, epoch=3), so it encodes observed scheduling rather than the invariant; and the handoff reply exposes no to_epoch, so the test's own landed_as ledger records <nil>.
findings.6_truthfulness_of_claims: (a) The surviving mutation_selfcheck_round2.json IS internally consistent with the 24-id roster: for all eight mutants len(card_rows_red) equals 24 minus passing_card_rows exactly, every red id is a roster member, and seven of eight anchors still occur exactly once in the delivered file (the eighth occurs seven times - P-W0602-8). The replaced invalid face is no longer on disk, so its content is a claim I cannot open; but its stated mechanism (a relative GOPATH making every go test exit 2 before emitting a row) is precisely the trap my own driver avoided by taking GOPATH/GOCACHE absolute from test.context.fixed_env, and two of its seven caught rows reproduce under my hands. (b) CONFIRMED, not merely reasoned: internal/store/sqlite.go:35 sets db.SetMaxOpenConns(1); the surviving attempt9 stack shows the test goroutine parked in database/sql.(*DB).conn at session_w0602_test.go:322 with a live *Tx.awaitDone frame; my probe reproduced the same starvation as a context deadline in 2.2s. The committed fix (seal inside a transaction closed before the next service call) is what the test now does. (c) The count is TRUE - I measured 0 domain_objects rows of kind 'Project' for the orchestration fixture project and 0 Run rows for a claimed task id. Seeding a Project row plus its Run rows is therefore not a fixture that proves nothing: it is the same substrate the accepted contracts check seeds at tests/contracts/check/main.go:867-869, the writer is a real provisioned principal with a real grant, every refusal comes from the service re-reading the store, and the gap is published as a measured id instead of smoothed over. Its only weakness is the self-compared slot. (d) The race row is a genuine no-lost-update check, not a row loosened until green: CONCURRENT-CLAIMS compares the stored epoch against 1+landed, where landed is counted independently of the epoch, so a lost update would show; the earlier 'exactly one success' expectation was a wrong belief about a serialised store, not a real invariant. The honest limit is that the store serialises, so the two goroutines can never interleave a read-modify-write: the row proves CAS-correctness under serialisation, not behaviour under true concurrency, and its RACE-LOSER companion is scheduling-dependent.

problems.statement: W06-02-RACE-LOSER-CANNOT-WRITE hard-codes STALE_WRITER_EPOCH for both epochs 1 and 2, which is only the true answer when both racing claims land and the session sits at epoch 3; if the store ever refused one claim, the loser's epoch-2 write would be refused WRITER_BUSY and the row would go red for a reason unrelated to a lost update.

problems.statement: The receipt lists TestW13MilestoneGates, TestW13GoalMilestone and TestW17UpgradeActiveRecovery as one undifferentiated COMMAND_FAILED row attributed to 'pre-existing', but the W13 pair are loopback flakes that PASS in isolation while only the W17 test fails deterministically, so the row as written invites someone to hunt a W13 bug that does not exist.
problems.evidence: frozen domain_full_suite_with_pre_existing_failures.txt lines 935-945 show the W13 failures as 'dial tcp 127.0.0.1:178xx ... connectex' fixture-listener refusals at workbench_security_test.go:19/:57; my `go test ./internal/domain -run '^(TestW13MilestoneGates|TestW13GoalMilestone)$' -count=1` returned EXIT=0 'ok 1.345s'; TestW17UpgradeActiveRecovery returns 'no such table: runtime_dispatches' every time, including in isolation.

ruling_on_the_mutation_that_crashed: M1-ignore-live-run-gate is correctly classified as a CRASHED, ILL-FORMED MUTANT, and it is not a survivor: the live-run handoff gate it tried to neutralise is falsifiable and I killed it. Their replacement text dropped the only read of the local `settled`, so the package never compiled ('internal\domain\session_service.go:202:10: declared and not used: settled'), the run emitted 0 rows and credited nothing - the executor recorded that honestly instead of scoring it as a catch or dropping it, and stated the consequence ('the gate ... is therefore still unmeasured by mutation'). I re-formed the same guard so it compiles: emptying `liveRunStatuses` (session_service.go:34) gives EXIT=1, 4 rows emitted, 3 PASS, 21 of the 24 roster ids red, with the FIRST failure exactly at W06-02-TAKEOVER-REFUSED-WHILE-RUN-LIVE (the 409 STOP_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED the id demands is no longer produced). So the live-run gate is NOT unkillable, the executor simply got the mutant wrong, and after this review all eight guards the matrix names are measured killable, the survivor count is zero, and no obligation stays open on M1. One caution travels with the ruling: the gate is only as strong as the run row it reads. My probe shows OpenClientSession accepts a run_id with no domain_objects Run row - the v2.4 index validates only the Project row - and a takeover of such a session then answers 404 NOT_FOUND, a branch no id covers. The gate is sound against the store it is given; it does not verify that the run it gates actually exists.
reservations_carried_on_the_registration: R1: writer attribution in internal/domain/session_service.go is by caller-supplied epoch and client id, both readable by any principal holding a grant on the project; obligation VB-4 remains UNBOUND and was not disclosed by this card. These 24 rows may not be cited for any multi-principal or LIVE claim.

R2: ConfirmRunStop has no idempotent replay path - a duplicate stop confirmation returns a raw UNIQUE-constraint error (Fault status 0, empty code). The event ledger stays correct (one RUN_STOP_CONFIRMED event, transaction rolled back), but the reply does not converge. Fix plus a named refusal id is owed.

R3: six delivered guards are unasserted although they behave correctly today: the grant checks on ConfirmRunStop, OpenClientSession, WriteAsWriter, SessionEvents and ListClientSessions, the sealed-session gate on the write path, the two limit-above-200 refusals, the four unknown-session NOT_FOUND branches and the runState 404 for a dangling run_id. Neutralising them keeps 24/24 green.

R4: the session surface is reachable from nothing but its own test - no file outside internal/domain/session*.{go} calls any of the seven methods - and session.handoff / session.list still answer NOT_IMPLEMENTED over the protocol envelope in client_protocol.go (accepted W03-02). Obligation W06-02-protocol-dispatcher-route is owed and is not yet in checkpoint.open_obligations_before_next_card.

R5: context_selector_parity_rev18.json describes the pre-final test face (312, missing the last two ids). The accepted-card neighbours were verified directly by this review (282 and 282 with identical id sets); that verification, not the parity file, is what the row rests on.

R6: the registry append (rev 17->18, digest f3555ad8cee2...) moved digests pinned by the ACCEPTED W06-01 row. The drift is recorded in a new erratum and no accepted evidence was edited, but the erratum's NO-ROW labels and its 15-file list are imprecise (measured: 17 files, 149 occurrences).

R7: fixture-level measurement only. store.Open pins the pool to one connection (internal/store/sqlite.go:35), so the race rows prove CAS correctness under serialisation, not under true concurrent interleaving; W06-02-INDEX-SUBSTRATE-GAP-MEASURED cannot fail on its Project-row half; W06-02-RACE-LOSER-CANNOT-WRITE encodes the observed landed=2 scheduling.
R8: card-level increment only. Parent W06 and W06-99 are not accepted, formal cases C01, C04 and C26 are signed by no one here, and the mode is DEVELOPMENT/FIXTURE, not LIVE.
limitations: I did not run the full test.context program with every phase (the ~350-400s face); I ran the four registered selectors this review turns on and compared them at id-set level, which is the narrower question the card poses.

I did not re-run the domain full suite (468s in the frozen log) and did not reproduce the W13 pair's flake under load; that they pass in isolation is measured, while their failing only inside the long suite rests on the frozen log plus the checkpoint's pre-existing environment entry.

I did not re-perform the executor's remove-two-files-and-rerun proof, because that would have meant moving delivered files; I substituted the mechanical coupling proof (no external reference to any new symbol, no init(), one package-level map literal) plus per-test isolation runs.

The discarded first mutation matrix is not on disk, so its all-crashed face is verified by mechanism (absolute versus relative GOPATH in fixed_env) and by the surviving file's internal consistency, not by inspection.

I did not mutate the accepted primitives themselves (MapClientSession, HandoffEpoch, AdvanceWatermark, Seal, EnsureClientSessionFence) - they belong to W03-01/W03-02 and their digests are pinned - so the epoch-regression and fence rows are credited to the accepted fence, which is what the test claims.

I measured nothing over a real socket, CLI or Desktop: no protocol envelope round-trip, no session.handoff route, no reconnect against a live process. Those are reservation R4 and the parent gate's business.
Cost is not measurable from here: charged_events is a field this card writes on its own reply, not a cost-ledger entry, so 费用收敛 is verified only as 'one outbox event and one idempotency row per key'.
I did not audit the 203-entry obligation register beyond searching it for this card's names, and I never modified step_state.json or checkpoint.json.
